notes:
Prospect builds a VS Code extension that surfaces streaming inline completions + block generation. Heavy focus on latency for inline suggestions (target: median RTT <100ms from keypress to first token). Key ask: server-side streaming with token-level deltas and ability to terminate streams mid-generation.

Auth/profile: extension has anonymous OSS tier + paid org tier. Need per-user and per-installation quotas, lightweight token rotation for client apps, and server-side rate limiting hooks. CTO quote on call: 'We cannot force users into a login flow for basic completions; need ephemeral tokens + throttles.'

Security/compliance: enterprise buyers demand SSO (SAML + SCIM), SOC2 attestation, audit logs per request, KMS integration for customer keys, and EU data residency for large accounts. Asking whether Redwood Private/VPC can be used for managed enterprise hosting.

POC requirements: 2-week perf evaluation with extension in Canary; scripted workload includes 1k concurrent active editors (short bursts), average prompt length 40 tokens, follow-up context retention (KV cache) for multi-line completions. Need measuring hooks: per-token latency histogram, dropped-stream counts, cold-start p99.

Integration notes: wants model-version pinning per channel/release (so we can A/B plugin releases), automatic fallback to smaller model when Dedicated pool saturated, and traffic routing by region. Cost sensitivity for OSS users — will use Optimize suggestions (quantization + batching) to reduce per-token cost.

Commercial: mid-market bundle expected; first-year ARR target $60k if SSO+dedicated upsell works. CSM indicates renewals tied to latency SLO and audit log retention.

Stated blockers: SSO timelines (customer legal), detailed SLA for median token latency, and marketplace requirements for VS Code extension auth flow.
